output.title: When search becomes a workflow decision
output.body:
If you are rethinking search behaviour in a small business, start with one question: are people repeatedly searching your own business material, or the open web? That difference matters. Repeated searching through customer emails, past invoices, product specs, or help-desk notes is a workflow problem. Random web research usually is not.

For an owner-operator, the practical threshold is simple: if that internal searching is taking a noticeable slice of the week and the result should be faster replies, fewer errors, or less back-and-forth, it is worth treating as a bounded automation decision. Not a grand AI strategy. Just one repeatable task.

The control is document readiness. A knowledge assistant only makes sense when the useful material already exists in machine-readable form, such as MD, PDF, or structured data. Bareni has a self-built demo that retrieves from approved company documents rather than the open web, on synthetic data. OCR, scan ingestion, billing, and rate limiting are not working in that demo.

Keep human approval in place if search output influences customer communication or a business decision. The system can propose; the owner decides. That is Bareni's policy for high-risk decisions, not a warranty.

One practical next step is a free 30-minute diagnostic: map one recurring search task on paper, check whether the source material is ready, and decide whether final review still needs to stay with the owner. If yes, you have a bounded workflow worth testing.
